title: Mindy Kaling's LA Restaurant Guide Spans Ethiopian, Korean BBQ and Wendy's
excerpt: The actress and creator shared her favorite Los Angeles spots with The Infatuation, from a South Indian gem in Woodland Hills to a Farmers Market donut counter she calls the best in America.
body:
• Mindy Kaling shared her 10 favorite Los Angeles restaurants with The Infatuation, spanning Ethiopian, South Indian, Armenian, Korean BBQ, and Mexican cuisines — plus Wendy's.
  • Chennai Tiffins in Woodland Hills earned a spotlight for its idli sambar, vadas, and dosas, which Kaling called "deeply comforting South Indian food that's weirdly hard to find in Hollywood."
  • The list reflects two decades of eating across LA, from longtime family spots like Carousel Restaurant in Glendale to writers' room staples like Sonoratown.
  • Kaling's new Hulu series "Not Suitable For Work" premieres as the latest installment in what she describes as a trilogy of shows about her younger years.

Two Decades of Eating in LA

Mindy Kaling has lived in Los Angeles for more than 20 years. In that time, the Emmy-nominated writer, actress, and creator behind The Mindy Project, Never Have I Ever, The Office, and Running Point has assembled a restaurant rotation that tells you as much about her life in the city as any résumé.

https://www.instagram.com/p/Dax34zxFF61/

In a guide published by The Infatuation, Kaling walked through her 10 go-to spots — a list that bounces from a Woodland Hills South Indian restaurant she visits with her father to the Wendy's on Sunset and La Brea where she orders a spicy chicken sandwich after a bad day. It's not a curated influencer list. It reads like a diary.

The South Indian Spot Worth the Drive

Chennai Tiffins in Woodland Hills occupies a special place in Kaling's rotation, not just for the food but for the ritual around it. She drives there with her father, using the uninterrupted hour in the car to catch up on what he's watching on YouTube — "usually travel videos or someone explaining the health benefits of obscure berries," she told The Infatuation.

"The idli sambar, vadas, and dosas here are incredible, and it's the kind of deeply comforting South Indian food that's weirdly hard to find in Hollywood. This place absolutely slaps."

— Mindy Kaling

For diaspora foodies who know the frustration of searching for authentic South Indian tiffin food in American cities, the endorsement carries weight. Chennai Tiffins represents a category of restaurant — modest, family-run, deeply specific to a regional cuisine — that rarely gets mainstream attention but sustains communities.

A Family History at Carousel Restaurant

Kaling's list carries personal history. Carousel Restaurant in Glendale dates back to her earliest days in LA, when she, her mother, and her father would visit after shopping trips to IKEA in Burbank. The restaurant, an Armenian institution, serves dishes she still orders two decades later: Albaloo Polo (sour cherry rice), fatayer (cheese boreg), muhammara (roasted red pepper and walnut dip), and lula kebab.

"We'd drive home completely delirious and overfed, then unpack the car while they asked questions about this new remake of the British Office," she recalled.

The Writers' Room Test

Comedy writers' rooms are, by Kaling's account, notoriously difficult to feed. "Picking lunch is usually a nightmare because comedy writers are incredibly opinionated people who all become food critics at noon," she said. The one place that achieves consensus: Sonoratown, specifically for its chivichanga — shredded chicken, beans, cheese, and flour tortillas made with lard.

She issued a warning: "You can really only have one, otherwise you will absolutely fall asleep during an afternoon rewrite, which I have learned the hard way."

Ethiopian, Korean BBQ, and a Donut Counter

The rest of Kaling's list reads like a cross-section of LA's immigrant food landscape. Meals by Genet, an Ethiopian restaurant, earns her highest praise — she said she could eat there three times a week for the rest of her life. She always orders the vegetarian combination, beef tibs, and foul, a spicy bean dip. The chef and owner, Genet, has become a personal friend, and Kaling once spotted Meryl Streep eating injera with her hands there.

Soot Bull Jip, a Korean BBQ spot with charcoal grills, gets the nod for smoky, sweet ribs and what Kaling calls "the perfect contrast" of cold, crunchy bean sprout banchan. Saffy's, a Middle Eastern kebab spot in East Hollywood, earns her recommendation for its red snapper tagine and beef skewers.

Bob's Coffee & Doughnuts at the Original Farmers Market provides what she calls "maybe my favorite donut in America" — the raspberry-filled variety. Valerie Confections rounds out the list with a black sesame cake made from devil's food cake, black sesame buttercream, raspberry jam, and macadamia croquant.

And Then There's Wendy's

The final entry is Wendy's. Spicy chicken sandwich, baked potato and chili, a Frosty, and on catastrophic days, a Baconator. Kaling's description of the Sunset and La Brea location — "aspiring actors, night nurses, comedy assistants, club girls in tiny skirts holding giant Diet Cokes, dads driving home from set" — captures a specific, unglamorous slice of LA that rarely makes restaurant guides.

Kaling's new series, Not Suitable For Work, is now streaming on Hulu. Set in New York, it's loosely based on her own coming-of-age experience in her early twenties and what she describes as the third part of a trilogy that began with The Mindy Project and continued with Never Have I Ever.
